title: Rust: Return Values
description: Return values from functions, including multiple return types and Option/Result.

steps.title: Return a Value
steps.description: Write a function `get_forty_two() -> i32` that returns 42. Call and print it.
hints: The return type is specified after `->`.
The value `42` is the last expression (no semicolon, no `return`).

steps.title: Return Tuple
steps.description: Write a function `min_max(arr: &[i32]) -> (i32, i32)` that returns the minimum and maximum of a slice. Call with `[3, 1, 7, 2, 9]`.

steps.title: Return Option
steps.description: Write a function `safe_divide(a: f64, b: f64) -> Option<f64>` that returns `None` if b is 0, else `Some(a/b)`. Call and print both cases.
hints: `Option` represents a value that might be absent.

verification.failureMessage: Return Some for valid division and None for division by zero.

steps.title: Return Result
steps.description: Write a function `parse_int(s: &str) -> Result<i32, String>` that parses a string to i32. Print success or error for `"42"` and `"abc"`.
hints: Return `Ok(value)` on success and `Err(msg)` on failure.

verification.failureMessage: Handle both valid and invalid string parsing.

steps.title: Return String
steps.description: Write a function `greet(name: &str) -> String` that returns a greeting like `"Hello, NAME!"`. Call and print.
hints: The caller owns the returned String.

verification.failureMessage: Write greet() that returns and prints a greeting string.
